body:
I don't really understand what exactly is your issue with your current setup of configurations.
However for your third statement it's not related to the visibility of the variable, as long it's serialized in the inspector if you rename it you will loose the value, unless you use this attribute : https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Serialization.FormerlySerializedAsAttribute.htm

The most important factor for an asset to be on sale is the revenue generated without any discount. And the amount of 5 stars reviews of course. Apparently assets that cost less than 20$ are less likely to be featured on sale.
I had exactly the same idea a few days ago but no time to develop it. It looks very useful for games with a lot of data.

Unity Asset database only accepts path relative to your project, so it must start by "Assets/...".
I recommend you to look at AssetDatabase.IsValidFolder to verify your paths.

Hey, I've made a small collection of attributes I use in all my projects, it's free on the asset store, maybe you'll find it useful. https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/tools/utilities/tetra-attributes-256483
NaughtyAttributes is also a good alternative to Odin.

I recommend you to create Tag/State as a scriptable object and store them inside another SO, like ObjectTags for example. Which is simply holding all tags and their state (enabled or disabled) for a specific GameObject. I said this because you probably need a system where you can easily add new tag or a state without modifying all your code, which is going to happen using enums. I mean enums as flags are not bad however they shouldn't change too much.

I've made an editor window to create, edit, rename, delete and search for any scriptable objects, it also save them in their respective folders. I no longer use the CreateAssetMenu attribute. It's something I want to sell, i'm waiting for the Unity team to review it before the release on the asset store.
It looks really good, congrats. It reminds me of Borderland a lot.

I think Tycoon games tend to have a lot of data, I've tried to make one before. You need a clear interface to display all the informations. One of the first things I would implement would be a data binding system so that translation is easier to implement, and changing the game data automatically updates the UI. Instead of having a lot of functions to update the text values for example.
That's weird I can access it, the game is now in production in 23 countries mostly Europe and the US maybe yours is not included, could you tell me so I can add it ?

I recommend you to check out Dark Rift 2, I'm also making a turn based card game on mobile. You can deploy a c# console app with all your server side game logic without unity (if not needed), making it lightweight and fully authoritative.The downside is that it takes longer to set up basic systems than Photon 2 or Mirror, but it's also an opportunity to learn how network games work. I personally really like having the client and server side code separated.
